#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# Testing Data - Main Agent and testing sub agent both should log testing data below this section

Enter them manually, or try again shortly.' ROOT CAUSE (two issues): (1) resolveCloudflareNameservers() only looked at the provider /domains list and the /dns records — but when a domain is on CUSTOM/registrar NS (e.g. dnsimple/openprovider) neither source contains the Cloudflare NS, so it returned [] -> 400 cloudflare_ns_unavailable. (2) Even after resolving, the upstream PUT /dns/:domain/nameservers is SLOW (~47s measured) and exceeded our 30s axios timeout -> 502 'timeout of 30000ms exceeded'. FIX: (a) resolveCloudflareNameservers now first calls GET /hosting/:user/domains/ns-status?domain=<domain> (using any reseller-owned hosting account as the auth context) which returns the domain's Cloudflare ZONE nameservers even when the registrar points elsewhere (verified: returns anderson/leanna.ns.cloudflare.com for namewords.sbs in 0.56s); falls back to the old /domains + /dns-records sources. (b) New applyNameservers() responds OPTIMISTICALLY after an 18s grace window with HTTP 202 {success:true, applying:true, nameservers:[...], reset_to_default/ns_choice} while the slow provider PUT (120s client timeout) completes in the background — so the frontend (30s axios budget) no longer times out. Custom-NS save uses the same path (also previously timed out). Frontend DnsManagerNomadly.jsx: saveNameservers/resetToDefault now show an 'applying — up to a minute' message on 202 and optimistically set the NS badge from res.nameservers. Legit x-api-key clients are unaffected (they send no bearer token → currentUser's no-token branch → soft next()). Only route using bare currentUser without requireAuth is /checkout quote (optional auth): a guest has no token (works); an expired token now yields 401 (prompts re-login) which is acceptable. Lint clean, backend restarted, health mode=live. VERIFY: invalid bearer → 401 (not 500) on a protected route; valid login still 200; banned/session behavior unchanged."

A safety-net cron (app/jobs/provisioningWorker.js, every 1 min) reclaims any order left in provisioning pending/processing whose lock is null or >5min old. processOrder is idempotent + lock-guarded (atomic findOneAndUpdate claim on provisioning+provisioningLockedAt) so the in-request kick-off and the cron never double-provision. Per-item cash/points are split at creation (cash_charged_usd/points_charged_usd, rounding reconciled on the last item) so items can be refunded/retried independently. On a failed item the worker refunds its committed cash to the wallet + restores its points and sets item.refunded_usd. recomputeOrderFinancials reconciles order.charged_usd/refunded_usd/points_earned (idempotent points delta) and status (paid/partial/failed) at the end. NEW ENDPOINTS: GET /api/v1/checkout/orders/:id/status (lightweight poll; best-effort live provider sync via GET /vps|/rdp/:id and GET /hosting/:user — no-op in dry_run since there are no provider ids; returns {provisioning, settled, status, items:[{idx,type,title,status,live_status,message,provider_id,provider_username,panel_url,server_ip,refunded_usd,attempts,price_usd}], charged_usd, refunded_usd, points_earned, wallet_balance_usd}). POST /api/v1/checkout/orders/:id/items/:idx/retry (ownership-gated; only a 'failed' item; re-debits item.price_usd cash then re-provisions; 402 with shortfall if wallet can't cover; 409 not_retryable if item isn't failed).   - task: "Idempotency hardening for DynoPay webhook and poller (crypto credits)"
    implemented: true

    status_history:
      - working: "NA"
        agent: "main"
        comment: "IDEMPOTENCY HARDENING — ensure the DynoPay WEBHOOK and the getPaymentStatus POLLER can never double-credit the same payment. What changed: both credit paths (webhook handleDynoPaymentWebhook + poller creditWalletTopup used by /wallet/crypto-topup/:id/status) now set Transaction.idempotencyKey = `dynopay:<payment_id>` and there is a UNIQUE SPARSE index on transactions.idempotencyKey (verified present). A duplicate credit for the same payment id is blocked both by a read-check and by the DB unique index. IMPORTANT: do NOT touch the buyer wallet (real $60). Use a FRESH throwaway user. TESTS: (1) Register a new unique user (POST /api/v1/auth/register {email,password,passwordConfirmation}); get its Mongo _id (query the users collection by that email) and its login token. (2) Simulate a confirmed crypto payment via the webhook (public route, GET): GET /api/v1/wallet/dynocheckout-webhook?uid=<userId>&amt=10&fe=wallet&status=successful&base_amount=10&payment_id=<UUID_A>&transaction_id=<UUID_A>&transaction_reference=<UUID_A>&payment_mode=CRYPTO → EXPECT 200 {success:true, message contains 'added to wallet'}. Then GET /api/v1/wallet/get (Bearer that user) → wallet USD == 10; and exactly ONE dynocash credit in /api/v1/wallet/transactions. (3) REPLAY the exact same webhook (same UUID_A) → EXPECT 200 but message 'already ... added'; wallet STILL 10; STILL exactly one dynocash credit; and in DB exactly ONE transaction has idempotencyKey 'dynopay:<UUID_A>'. (4) CONTROL: call the webhook with a DIFFERENT payment_id UUID_B & amt=5 & base_amount=5 → credits; wallet now 15 (distinct payments are NOT blocked). (5) CROSS-PATH NOTE (assurance, no real crypto): the poller (creditWalletTopup) uses the SAME idempotencyKey `dynopay:<payment_id>`, so once the webhook credits UUID_A, a poller credit for the same id would hit the unique index and be skipped — you can confirm the unique+sparse index exists on transactions.idempotencyKey. (6) REGRESSION: POST /api/v1/wallet/crypto-topup (Bearer buyer) {amount:15,currency:'ETH'} → still 201 with address (does NOT credit); GET /api/v1/payment/getSupportedCurrency → 200. Do NOT reset any wallet. Report PASS/FAIL per item with HTTP status + observed wallet balances and dynocash credit counts."

metadata:
  created_by: "main_agent"
  version: "1.0"
  test_sequence: 23
  run_ui: true

test_plan:
  current_focus:
    - "DNS Manager: reset-to-default nameservers (fix cloudflare_ns_unavailable + slow-PUT timeout)"
  stuck_tasks: []
  test_all: false
  test_priority: "high_first"

agent_communication:
  - agent: "main"
    message: "TEST BACKEND ONLY — DNS Manager nameserver reset-to-default fix. Focus task: 'DNS Manager: reset-to-default nameservers ...'. SETUP (idempotent): `cd /app/backend && node scripts/seed_filemanager_tester.js` -> user filemanager.tester@nameword.local / FileMgr!Test123 who OWNS the REAL domain namewords.sbs. Login: POST /api/v1/auth/login {email,password} -> Authorization: Bearer token. IMPORTANT: the upstream registrar NS change is genuinely SLOW (~45s); our endpoint responds OPTIMISTICALLY at ~18s with HTTP 202 {applying:true} while it finishes in the background — so use a per-request timeout of at least 40s, and treat BOTH 200 and 202 as success. This mutates a REAL (reseller-owned test) domain — that is expected and desired; leave it on default at the end. STEPS (base /api/v1/reseller): (1) THE BUG FIX — PUT /dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {mode:'default'} -> MUST be 200 or 202 with success:true, ns_choice:'cloudflare', reset_to_default:true, and nameservers being 2 cloudflare hostnames (…ns.cloudflare.com). It MUST NOT return 400 cloudflare_ns_unavailable and MUST NOT return 502 timeout. (2) CUSTOM then DEFAULT round-trip: PUT /dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {nameservers:['ns1.dnsimple.com','ns2.dnsimple.com']} -> 200/202 success (ns_choice:'custom', nameservers echoed); then PUT {mode:'default'} again -> 200/202 with the cloudflare nameservers. (3) VALIDATION: PUT {nameservers:['only-one.com']} -> 400 invalid_nameservers. (4) OWNERSHIP/AUTH: PUT {mode:'default'} with NO Authorization header -> blocked 401/400 (must NOT reach provider); as this user, PUT /dns/<a-domain-you-don't-own e.g. example-not-owned.com>/nameservers {mode:'default'} -> 403/blocked. (5) NO REGRESSION: GET /api/v1/reseller/health -> 200 mode:live. Report exact HTTP codes + the nameservers array returned for the default resets. Note: the provider is external (1.speechcue.com); the 202-then-background behavior is by design, not a bug."
  - agent: "testing"
    message: "✅ CPANEL FILE MANAGER BACKEND TEST COMPLETE - ALL CRITICAL TESTS PASSED (9/10, 90% SUCCESS RATE). Comprehensive testing via backend_filemanager_test.py against LIVE Nomadly reseller provider (1.speechcue.com). Test account: filemanager.tester@nameword.local / FileMgr!Test123 (owns REAL cPanel account 'nbayftest', domain testingbays.sbs). SAFETY VERIFIED: All writes performed inside throwaway temp directory /apitest_658273 and cleaned up at end. NO files in /public_html were touched or deleted. CRITICAL SUCCESS: THE ONE-TAP UNZIP ENDPOINT (POST /files/unzip) IS FULLY WORKING AGAINST THE LIVE PROVIDER. Response: HTTP 200 {status:1, action:'files.unzip', uploaded:{fileName:'site.zip', bytes:139}, extracted:{src:'...site.zip', dest:'...'}, archiveRemoved:true, listing:['hello.txt','note.txt'], added:['hello.txt'], healed:true, healed_via:'whm-fallback'}. All checks passed: action=='files.unzip' ✓, archiveRemoved==true ✓, added is non-empty ✓, listing is non-empty ✓, extracted file (hello.txt) appears in added/listing ✓. The endpoint correctly uploads base64 archive, extracts it, removes the archive file, and returns both listing and added files in a single call. DETAILED RESULTS: ✅ STEP 1 (GET /files listing): HTTP 200, real listing with 21 entries (status:1, data is non-empty array). ✅ STEP 2 (POST /files/mkdir): HTTP 200, temp directory created. ✅ STEP 3 (POST /files/upload): HTTP 200, note.txt uploaded. ✅ STEP 4 (POST /files/unzip ONE-TAP): HTTP 200, ALL CHECKS PASSED (see above). ✅ STEP 5 (TWO-STEP upload+extract): HTTP 200 for both operations. ⚠️ STEP 6 (GET /files verify): HTTP 200, files exist but test script had minor parsing issue (looked for 'name' key but API returns 'file' key) - this is a test script issue, NOT an API issue. ✅ STEP 7 (DELETE cleanup): HTTP 200, temp directory deleted. ✅ STEP 8a (no auth header): HTTP 400, blocked without token (did NOT reach provider). ✅ STEP 8b (cross-owner access): HTTP 403 {error:'forbidden'} for non-owned account. ✅ STEP 9 (health check): HTTP 200 {mode:'live'}. CRITICAL VERIFICATION: (1) ONE-TAP UNZIP is production-ready and working perfectly. (2) All file operations work through our backend proxy to LIVE provider. (3) Ownership-scoping prevents cross-customer access (403). (4) Auth guard blocks unauthenticated requests (400). (5) Provider latency acceptable (all ops within 30s). (6) Provider is LIVE (mode='live'). (7) Safety verified: temp dir created/used/deleted, NO /public_html files touched. NO MAJOR ISSUES FOUND. cPanel File Manager backend proxy is FULLY WORKING against LIVE Nomadly reseller provider. The NEW one-tap /files/unzip endpoint is production-ready."

  - agent: "main"
    message: "[archived — NS bundle backend-test brief, since VERIFIED 5/5] Context: when a domain is bought TOGETHER with a hosting plan in the same order, the Anti-Red cPanel hosting serves the site through its own Cloudflare zone and returns the nameservers the domain must use. Previously the domain was registered with the buyer's ns_choice (cloudflare/registrar/custom) and the hosting NS were never applied to the domain -> the buyer's NS choice could break the hosting. FIX in /app/backend/app/controllers/checkout/CheckoutController.js: (1) provisionItem(domain) now takes opts.skipCustomNs — when true it registers with ns_choice 'cloudflare' and does NOT send/apply the buyer's custom NS. (2) processOrder builds a set of domains that also have a hosting item in the SAME order; for those domain items it sets item.ns_managed_by='hosting' and passes skipCustomNs=true. (3) After provisioning, a live-mode-only reconciliation pass points each hosting-bundled domain's nameservers to the hosting account's nameservers via PUT /dns/:domain/nameservers. Order model gained item field ns_managed_by ('user'|'hosting'). NOTE: reseller is in dry_run (GET /api/v1/reseller/health mode=dry_run) so nothing is provisioned/charged upstream and the live NS PUT will NOT run — that is EXPECTED. WHAT TO VERIFY via POST /api/v1/checkout/orders (login first: POST /api/v1/auth/login, seeded buyer buyer@nameword.local / Buyer@12345 if present, else register a fresh user and top up is not needed for dry_run test_mode): submit an order with items [{type:'domain',domain:'<fresh-random>.com',ns_choice:'custom',nameservers:['ns1.evil.com','ns2.evil.com']},{type:'hosting',domain:'<same-domain>',plan_id:'golden-monthly'}] and a fresh client_order_id (uuid). EXPECT: 201/200; the DOMAIN order item must come back with ns_managed_by='hosting' and ns_choice effectively cloudflare (the buyer's custom evil NS must NOT be honored). Also submit a control order with ONLY a domain (ns_choice:'custom', 2 valid NS, no hosting) -> that domain item must remain ns_managed_by='user' and keep its custom NS. Confirm no boot/route regressions (GET /api/v1/reseller/health 200). Use fresh random domains each run to avoid 409. dry_run test_mode statuses are a PASS, not a bug."

## ================= SESSION 2025-07: Duplicate-hosting fix + File Manager rebuild =================
backend:
  - task: "Problem 1: De-duplicate hosting accounts (ownership.ownedList)"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "app/services/ownership.js"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
      - working: "NA"
        agent: "main"
        comment: "BUG: account moxxcompany@gmail.com showed TWO hosting plans for the SAME website namewords.sbs — the real provisioned account (order NW-MU76E3UGXQBJ, status=active, cPanel user namea3a5) PLUS a leftover unpaid crypto attempt (order NW-MU75DOFYKYK5, order.status=awaiting_payment, item.status=pending, no provider_username). Root cause: ownedList counted 'pending' items from unpaid (awaiting_payment) orders, and the hosting dedupe key differed (provider_username vs domain) so the same site appeared twice. FIX in ownedList: (1) skip items whose parent order.status is not in [paid,partial,failed] (unpaid checkouts own nothing); (2) skip items with refunded_usd>0 that are not active; (3) dedupe hosting by WEBSITE (domain) and keep the highest ownScore (active+provider handle beats pending). Also ran idempotent scripts/cleanup_superseded_hosting.js which settled the abandoned order NW-MU75DOFYKYK5 (item+order -> failed). VERIFIED via scripts/verify_dedupe.js: ownedList(moxx,'hosting') now returns exactly 1 account (namea3a5). Please retest GET /api/v1/reseller/hosting (login moxxcompany@gmail.com / Onlygod123@) returns exactly ONE account (username namea3a5, domain namewords.sbs, active) and that other buyers' domain/vps/rdp lists are unaffected (buyer@nameword.local / Buyer@12345)."
      - working: true
        agent: "testing"
        comment: "✅ PROBLEM 1 FULLY PASSED (2/2 tests, 100% success rate). Comprehensive backend testing via /app/backend_test.py. TEST 1 (DUPLICATE FIX - THE KEY TEST): Login moxxcompany@gmail.com / Onlygod123@ -> GET /api/v1/reseller/hosting returned HTTP 200 with EXACTLY ONE account in the accounts array.   - task: "Problem 2: cPanel File Manager backend (body limit + proxy routes)"
    implemented: true
    working: false
    file: "app.js"
    stuck_count: 1
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
      - working: "NA"
        agent: "main"
        comment: "Raised express.json / urlencoded body limit from the 100kb default to 25mb so base64 file uploads and chunked-upload chunks are accepted (previously any non-tiny upload would 413). File Manager proxy routes already exist in resellerController HOSTING_MGMT_ROUTES (files, files/content, files/save, files/mkdir, files/rename, files/extract, files/compress, files/copy, files/move, DELETE files, files/upload, files/upload-chunk, files/upload-chunk/cancel) and are ownership-scoped via withOwnedHosting -> live for provisioned accounts. Test LIVE against moxx's namea3a5 (dir /public_html): GET /api/v1/reseller/hosting/namea3a5/files?dir=/public_html returns {status:1,data:[...]}; POST files/save then files/upload (small base64) then files/mkdir/rename/copy/move/compress/extract then DELETE files. Provider blocks .htaccess/.user.ini/.antired-challenge.php with 403 protected_file (expected). MySQL is 403 mysql_requires_monthly on the 7-day plan (expected, not a bug)."
      - working: false
        agent: "testing"
        comment: "❌ PROBLEM 2 PARTIALLY FAILED (2/12 file operations working, 10/12 failing with CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE). Comprehensive backend testing via /app/backend_test.py with full 12-step File Manager lifecycle test on username namea3a5, working dir /public_html. Login moxxcompany@gmail.com / Onlygod123@ successful. CRITICAL ISSUE: Most file operations return CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE (401/403) from the upstream cPanel provider, NOT from our backend code. The responses are NOT dry_run/test_mode envelopes - they are actual provider-side authentication errors. DETAILED RESULTS: ❌ STEP 1 (GET files list): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['<!DOCTYPE html>'], data:null, httpStatus:401, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 2 (POST files/save): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['<!DOCTYPE html>'], data:null, httpStatus:401, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 3 (GET files/content): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:[], data:null, httpStatus:401, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 4 (POST files/upload base64): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Request failed with status code 401'], data:null, httpStatus:401, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 5 (POST files/mkdir): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 6 (POST files/rename): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 7 (POST files/copy): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 8 (POST files/move): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 9 (POST files/compress): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ❌ STEP 10 (POST files/extract): HTTP 200 but body {status:0, errors:['Access denied'], data:null, httpStatus:403, code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'}. ✅ STEP 11 (POST files/upload-chunk, 2 chunks): Chunk 0 returned HTTP 200 {status:'chunk-received', uploadId:'nwtestchunk1', received:1, totalChunks:2}. Chunk 1 returned HTTP 200 {status:'complete', cpanelStatus:0, errors:['Request failed with status code 401'], code:'CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE'} BUT the file was created (confirmed by successful deletion in cleanup). The chunked upload endpoint works despite the auth error in the response. ✅ STEP 12 (DELETE files cleanup): All 4 items deleted successfully (nw_test_renamed.txt, nw_test_archive.zip, nw_chunk.txt, nw_test_dir). DELETE endpoint works correctly. ANALYSIS: (1) The backend code changes (25mb body limit + proxy routes) are correctly implemented - all requests reach the backend and are properly forwarded to the Nomadly provider. (2) The Nomadly provider's cPanel integration has authentication issues for most file operations (list, save, content, upload, mkdir, rename, copy, move, compress, extract). (3) The chunked upload endpoint (files/upload-chunk) and DELETE endpoint work correctly, suggesting they use different authentication methods (chunked upload uses WHM session authentication per the response 'via:whm-session' in first test run). (4) This is a PROVIDER-SIDE issue, not a backend code issue. The review request mentions 'GET /ssl may return an upstream CPANEL_AUTH_FAILURE (provider-side, not our app)' as an expected non-bug, and this appears to be a similar provider-side authentication problem affecting most file operations. RECOMMENDATION: Main agent should investigate the Nomadly provider's cPanel authentication configuration for the namea3a5 account. The cPanel credentials may need to be refreshed or the provider's WHM/cPanel API integration may need to be fixed. The backend code changes are working correctly - the issue is with the upstream provider's authentication."

## ================= SESSION 2026-09 (continuation): Nameserver default/custom toggle =================
backend:
  - task: "Nameservers: reset-to-default (Cloudflare) + custom via PUT /dns/:domain/nameservers"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "app/controllers/reseller/resellerController.js"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
      - working: "NA"
        agent: "main"
        comment: "Enhanced setNameservers so the UI can switch a domain BACK to its default (Cloudflare) nameservers, not just set custom ones. PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/:domain/nameservers now supports TWO modes: (1) CUSTOM (unchanged) — body {nameservers:[>=2]} is forwarded to Nomadly as-is; (2) DEFAULT — body {mode:'default'} (also accepts {ns_choice:'cloudflare'} or {default:true}) resolves the domain's Cloudflare-assigned nameservers server-side (via provider GET /domains, fallback to the Cloudflare zone's NS records from GET /dns/:domain/records) and PUTs them; if it can't find >=2 Cloudflare NS it returns 400 cloudflare_ns_unavailable. Ownership gate (withOwnedDomain) unchanged. Self-verified via curl: moxxcompany@gmail.com PUT {mode:'default'} on namewords.sbs -> 200 {nameservers:[anderson.ns.cloudflare.com, leanna.ns.cloudflare.com], updated:true, detail:{nameserverType:'cloudflare'}, ns_choice:'cloudflare', reset_to_default:true}. PLEASE RETEST SAFELY (namewords.sbs is a REAL live domain): (A) moxxcompany@gmail.com / Onlygod123@ -> PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {mode:'default'} => 200, nameservers = the two *.ns.cloudflare.com, updated:true (idempotent/safe — the domain is already on Cloudflare). (B) OWNERSHIP: buyer@nameword.local / Test@12345 -> same PUT on namewords.sbs => 403 forbidden (buyer does not own it). (C) INVALID: moxxcompany PUT {} (empty body) on namewords.sbs => a 4xx error (no mutation). DO NOT set real/bogus CUSTOM nameservers on namewords.sbs (that would move the live domain off Cloudflare) — only exercise mode:'default' + the 403 + the empty-body error."
      - working: true
        agent: "testing"
        comment: "✅ TESTED via backend_dns_nameserver_reset_test.py. ALL 4 TESTS PASSED (4/4, 100% success rate). Comprehensive testing of the DNS nameserver management endpoint (PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/:domain/nameservers) covering all SAFE scenarios specified in review_request. SAFETY VERIFIED: Only tested on namewords.sbs domain with mode:'default' (idempotent, already on Cloudflare). NO custom/bogus nameservers were set on this REAL live domain. TEST RESULTS: ✅ TEST A (RESET-TO-DEFAULT HAPPY PATH): Login as moxxcompany@gmail.com / Onlygod123@, PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {mode:'default'} returns HTTP 200 with ALL required fields: updated=true ✓, nameservers=['anderson.ns.cloudflare.com', 'leanna.ns.cloudflare.com'] ✓ (both Cloudflare nameservers present), ns_choice='cloudflare' ✓, reset_to_default=true ✓, detail.nameserverType='cloudflare' ✓. The mode:'default' reset functionality is WORKING CORRECTLY. ✅ TEST B (OWNERSHIP ENFORCEMENT): Login as buyer@nameword.local / Test@12345 (does NOT own namewords.sbs), PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {mode:'default'} returns HTTP 403 with error='forbidden', message='You don't have access to this domain.' ✓. Ownership-gating prevents cross-customer access. CRITICAL SECURITY VERIFIED. ✅ TEST C (INVALID/EMPTY BODY - NO MUTATION): Login as moxxcompany@gmail.com, PUT /api/v1/reseller/dns/namewords.sbs/nameservers {} (empty body) returns HTTP 400 with error='invalid_nameservers', message='Provide at least 2 nameservers: { \"nameservers\": [\"ns1...\",\"ns2...\"] }' ✓. Empty body correctly rejected with 4xx error, NO change applied. ✅ READ-ONLY SANITY CHECK: GET /api/v1/reseller/dns/namewords.sbs/records as moxxcompany returns HTTP 200 with source='cloudflare' ✓, records array with 2 NS records (leanna.ns.cloudflare.com, anderson.ns.cloudflare.com) ✓. DNS records endpoint working correctly. CRITICAL FUNCTIONALITY VERIFIED: (1) mode:'default' reset works correctly - returns 200 with Cloudflare nameservers, updated=true, ns_choice='cloudflare', reset_to_default=true. (2) Ownership-gating prevents unauthorized access - buyer cannot modify moxxcompany's domain (403 forbidden). (3) Invalid/empty body rejected with 400 error - no mutation applied.
